races.name: Scone Palace Jousting Tournament Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Trigg
runners_data.note: Superior rating but hold-up style may not suit the likely steady pace scenario with Harry Skelton needing to be patient.
runners_data.spotlight: Did well in bumpers and comfortably off the mark over hurdles at Uttoxeter (2m, good); this is tougher than that winnable race but he's well related and entitled to improve plenty more with racing.

runners_data.name: Saint Cunning
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making hurdles debut for a trainer with poor recent form, needs significant improvement from bumper fifth.
runners_data.comment: Killygowan might be the yard first strong but the betting will provide more clues
runners_data.spotlight: Ordinary form when fifth in a bumper here but did go off only 5-1 and he raced freely before weakening late on; could improve on that but clearly needs to.

runners_data.name: Kibris
runners_data.note: Course winner last month who should control the pace from the front, headgear retained suggests confidence.
runners_data.comment: Big shout at best but ended time with Joseph O'Brien on a low note
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat winner for Joseph O'Brien; 0-4 over hurdles for that yard but came good on stable debut (same ownership) with a narrow win over 2m here last month (good to soft); he would have won easier but for a late mistake; there are some stamina concerns over quite this far.

runners_data.name: Dolly Dior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner on hurdles debut but showed insufficient promise in bumpers to warrant strong support.
runners_data.comment: 40-1 and never seriously counted on good ground at Sedgefield earlier this month
runners_data.spotlight: Insufficient promise in two good-ground bumpers to warrant a second look here on hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Flying Ace
runners_data.note: Recent winner over hurdles with Sean Bowen up, prominent style suits expected race shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way on hurdle debut at Downpatrick; probably the one to beat
runners_data.spotlight: Only his second run over hurdles when making no mistake at odds-on in a good-ground 2m1f maiden at Cartmel 11 days ago; the RPR was modest but he did beat a useful Flat recruit and his yard has won three of the last four renewals of this race.

runners_data.name: Busted Springs
runners_data.note: Poor bumper form including being tailed off here last time, headgear addition unlikely to transform prospects.
runners_data.comment: Well held on last month's Ayr debut; has a tongue-tie added now
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off in bumpers at Ayr (heavy) and here (good to soft); huge odds both times.

runners_data.name: Brewdog
runners_data.note: Tailed off behind Kibris here 24 days ago, tendency to fade in the finish makes him essentially no-hope.
runners_data.comment: Failed to beat a rival in two bumpers last season; big outsider now hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: 300-1 when tailed off behind Kibris here 24 days ago; no appeal.

races.paceDynamic: Kibris will lead or sit handy early with no obvious pace pressure in this small field of seven. Flying Ace and Dolly Dior are likely to track behind him prominently, while Trigg and Saint Cunning will settle towards the rear given their hold-up styles. The pace should be steady rather than searching, allowing the race to develop into a tactical affair. This shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can position close to Kibris and kick when the pace lifts, rather than the hold-up horses who may struggle to make up ground from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kibris Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kibris maintains his recent course form and dictates from the front without serious pressure.
scenarios.body: The pace stays manageable allowing him to kick clear approaching the last, with Flying Ace best placed to follow him through. Hold-up horses struggle to close the gap as the leaders have too much left in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Flying Ace or other prominent runners put pressure on Kibris turning for home.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and allows the better-rated prominent runners to assert their class advantage. Trigg finds too much to do from his hold-up position despite his superior rating.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Rallies
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling and the race turns into a sprint from the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Trigg's superior class rating tells as he gets a strong ride from Harry Skelton to sweep past tiring leaders. The tactical nature allows Saint Cunning to also get involved late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Kibris fails to fire and the race becomes truly run with no obvious leader.
scenarios.body: Flying Ace inherits the lead by default but the messy pace allows an outsider like Saint Cunning to sneak through. The lack of rhythm disrupts all the fancied runners' usual patterns.

watchPoints.text: Kibris may get an uncontested lead if no other prominent runners challenge early, making him very difficult to peg back.
Flying Ace's recent Cartmel win produced a modest RPR but Sean Bowen's presence suggests confidence from the Elliott team.
Trigg's hold-up style could be problematic if Kibris sets a steady pace that doesn't come back to the field.
Saint Cunning raced freely in his bumper here, which could be an issue if he doesn't settle better over hurdles.
The Crawford trainer has both Kibris and Saint Cunning but current form figures show 0 wins from 6 runners in past 14 days.

races.name: Sun Racing The Home Of Racing Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Morandi Second
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 326 days off and 0-11 over hurdles suggests major improvement needed
runners_data.spotlight: 0-11 over hurdles and absent since weakening fifth at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last summer; current mark is workable but others have more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Storm The Dug
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer who won well over C&D in April, suits turning this into sprint finish
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer (albeit a maiden) who kept on from the rear for clear second behind Breadalbane Lass over C&D (good) on handicap hurdle debut in April; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Breadalbane Lass
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who beat Storm The Dug over C&D, benefits from slow early pace
runners_data.comment: Clear winner at Perth last month, her 12th hurdle run; 8lb higher here; still considered
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on too strongy for Storm The Dug over C&D (good) in April, getting off the mark over hurdles at the 12th attempt, but was well held (albeit on soft ground) at Hexham last month; others have more potential.

runners_data.name: Betteryouthanme
runners_data.note: Showed improvement last time at 2m4f, drop back to 2m could suit hold-up style
runners_data.comment: Struggled in three runs in maiden/novice company (huge prices) at Ayr, Wetherby, & Hexham.
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed improvement and travelled well for a long way when third here (2m4f, good to soft) on last month's handicap debut; may benefit from this drop back in trip; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Struth
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but struggled since Flat peak, tongue-tie addition may help jumping rhythm
runners_data.comment: Useful on Flat in prime but yet to better fair form over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on the Flat in his prime but well held when fifth on handicap hurdle debut at Kelso (2m2f, good; first-time tongue-tie) in April and showed no significant improvement in a subsequent C&D maiden; needs to up his game.

runners_data.name: Jack Dempsey
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who was pulled up here last time, question marks over current form
runners_data.comment: 0-7; steps back up in trip for h'cap debut and that should bring about some improvement.
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from break with fairly encouraging run in C&D novice in April but was pulled up in 2m4f handicap here last month and has a fair bit more to prove than some of these.

runners_data.name: Bouboule
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from wind operation, previous form suggests ability lurking
runners_data.comment: 17-race maiden; hopes are pinned on wind surgery prompting a major turnaround
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in Musselburgh maiden (1m7f, good to soft) in November but has looked out of sorts over hurdles and on the Flat in recent months (had wind op before latest run); needs to turn a corner.

runners_data.name: Allibaba
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with recent winning form for new yard, good ground form gives confidence
runners_data.comment: Made light of a 538-day absence to win for the first time at Market Rasen 12 days ago.
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from long absence with good-ground wins at Market Rasen and Warwick for new stable last month; should cope if the ground is softer here and might still be on the upgrade; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Blondina
runners_data.note: Basement mark maiden who fades in finish, lowest weight but concerning finishing pattern
runners_data.comment: Good 3rd at Musselburgh on first Flat run for the yard; she now has something to build on
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no significant promise in her three qualifying races over hurdles in January-March but makes handicap hurdle debut from a basement mark and returns to this code after winning on the Flat (1m4f; RPR 61) last month; interesting.

runners_data.name: Magic Gloves
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner in field, gets uncontested lead but heavy defeats last season worry
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in February but encouraging handicap debut prior to that; not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Promising fourth on handicap debut at Musselburgh (1m7f, soft) in December but suffered heavy defeats on final two starts last season, the latter over C&D, and needs subsequent wind op to have made a big difference.

runners_data.name: Karthala
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with solid recent third behind Allibaba, cheekpieces refitted successfully
runners_data.comment: Has shown in little in three runs over hurdles; makes his handicap hurdle debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Over 8l behind Alibaba when third at Warwick (2m, good; refitted cheekpieces) last month but that was still a pretty good start to his handicap hurdle career and further progress is possible.

runners_data.name: King Kodiak
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who can be clumsy jumper, mixed hurdles record but placed recently
runners_data.comment: Clumsy jumper with very mixed hurdling record; ran big race two starts ago, though
runners_data.spotlight: Placed off 5lb higher at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) in April but has very mixed record over hurdles and is sometimes a clumsy jumper; safely held on last two outings; others look much safer.

runners_data.name: Bray Dale
runners_data.note: Struggling hold-up type now 0-10 over hurdles, visor added but hard to fancy
runners_data.comment: Arrives here after a couple of heavy defeats and has lots to prove.
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled in Hexham seller last month (first-time visor) and is now 0-10 over hurdles; 2lb out of the weights here; difficult to enthuse over.

races.paceDynamic: Magic Gloves stands out as the only confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field, with all other runners holding up or racing midfield. This creates a scenario where Magic Gloves can dictate terms unopposed from the front, setting a comfortable gallop over 2 miles on good ground. With no pace pressure early, the race will develop into a sustained drive from the 3-furlong pole as the hold-up horses try to close the gap. This pace shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with proven finishing kicks, as Magic Gloves may have enough left to resist late challengers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Magic Gloves Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Gloves gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the front-runner to conserve energy and build an unassailable advantage as the hold-up horses struggle to close the gap quickly enough. This rewards the one horse willing to make the running from the outset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and sets up a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their perfect scenario with a slow tempo allowing them to unleash their finishing kicks in the final 2 furlongs. Fresh legs and turn of foot become decisive over stamina and early positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Gloves sets steady fractions but gets pressured from 4 furlongs out
scenarios.body: The race develops into a proper test where horses with proven form at the trip can grind out the finish. This scenario rewards consistency and recent winning form over pure tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Gloves stops quickly or makes jumping errors under pressure
scenarios.body: The lack of alternative pace-setters creates chaos as reluctant leaders are forced forward, disrupting their preferred tactics. This opens the door for outsiders who can adapt to the changing race dynamics.

watchPoints.text: Magic Gloves must be watched for jumping fluency as any errors could derail the front-running tactics completely
Storm The Dug and Breadalbane Lass positioning early will indicate if they plan to make their move sooner than usual
Allibaba's jumping rhythm having returned from long absence will show if recent wins can translate here
The pace through the first mile will determine if this becomes a staying test or sprint finish
Any horse trying to track Magic Gloves early would completely change the tactical dynamic

races.name: Scone Palace International Horse Trials Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if pace is strong but changing yards after poor recent form is concerning
runners_data.comment: Return to hurdles could reignite a spark; possibly a few pounds too high in the handicap.
runners_data.spotlight: Won this two years ago and later added another handicap off this mark; however, he has rather lost his way and now kicks off for a new yard; enjoys good ground.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but recent flat run and 45-day break raises fitness questions
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on the Flat but she may need more of a stamina test than this
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth of six on the Flat last time out and beaten 22l here the time before that; a four-time winner in this discipline but reservations at the minute.

runners_data.name: Scriabin
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with 0-13 hurdles record but will ensure honest early gallop
runners_data.comment: 12-race maiden over hurdles but placed on three of four runs for this yard, including C&D
runners_data.spotlight: 0-3 on the Flat and 0-13 over hurdles, having had a few chances now in maidens and handicaps; has to raise his game.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but has been well beaten here twice since April suggesting weights caught up
runners_data.comment: 6lb higher than when winning readily at Hexham (2m) last October; this rates a tough test.
runners_data.spotlight: Progressed well last year but the signs are that she might be a shade high in the weights now after heavy defeats here since April.

runners_data.name: Scots Poet
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with recent good form and 5lb weight drop from Kelso win makes him dangerous
runners_data.comment: Won at Sedgefield and backed it up with good Hexham second 15 days ago; not taken lightly
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed multiple winner; he would have found the ground too soft when beaten by King Sacre at Hexham and then dug deep to win at Kelso (2m, good; 5lb lower); entitled to have some say.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner but 51-day gap and poor last hurdles effort are negatives
runners_data.comment: Ran well over hurdles two starts ago; handy mark on best 2025 Flat form; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Good fourth at Musselburgh in March but tailed off in his last run over hurdles and down the field on the Flat last week; others look more likely.

runners_data.name: Ailt An Chorrain
runners_data.note: Front-runner switching from blinkers to cheekpieces after 67-day break
runners_data.comment: In the frame on both starts since fitted with blinkers; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 2-6 over hurdles, though neither win came in a handicap; only one effort of note in five runs over fences and blinkers are replaced by cheekpieces; the stable probably has brighter prospects with Cosmic Soul.

runners_data.name: Largy Meadow
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with two handicap seconds, needed stronger pace last time here
runners_data.comment: Bustled up winner at Newcastle (2m4f, good; from 2lb lower) penultimate; PU over C&D since
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in the two handicaps he has completed and could have done with a truer pace when chasing home the market leader over 2m4f here last time; he's highly likely to get one here and he's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Soul
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on hat-trick after recent breakthrough, mark risen but in form
runners_data.comment: Readily landed the odds over C&D 13 days ago; hiked up 10lb now but still the one to beat
runners_data.spotlight: His hat-trick (2m1f-2m4f; good) has come at a cost mark-wise but it was all very straightforward last time at Sedgefield; something has clicked big time and he could deal with another 6lb.

runners_data.name: Alidam
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but fading finish pattern and 108-day absence are major concerns
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; fair third over 2m on h'cap debut; may do better up in trip with headgear tried
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French gelding; beaten 6l on handicap debut at Huntingdon (2m, soft) but failed to fire at Sedgefield in the new cheekpieces that are retained; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Prominent style with recent placed efforts, flat run Thursday wasn't too shabby
runners_data.comment: Twice placed over hurdles this spring and today's trip may be a good fit in this code
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 over hurdles but placed in his last two attempts and went very close at Carlisle in March (2m1f, good to soft); Thursday's Flat run when sixth wasn't too shoddy; can go well.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: Hold-up style returning from wind surgery but 50-1 debut performance was dire
runners_data.comment: Not obviously well treated off this opening mark but things may click at some point
runners_data.spotlight: In a good yard and returns from wind surgery, but she was 50-1 for her handicap debut here in April and performed accordingly.

runners_data.name: King Sacre
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with recent Hexham win, 9lb rise seems fair for progressive type
runners_data.comment: Unexposed; improved form when second on h'cap debut at Sedgefield last time; a possible
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in his first handicap (on good) and then made all the running on soft ground at Hexham, beating Scots Poet by some 17l; raised 9lb for that but he's far from exposed.

races.paceDynamic: Ailt An Chorrain and Scriabin will contest the early lead in this 13-runner field, with both horses having confirmed front-running tendencies. Their early battle should create an honest gallop over the 2m trip on good ground. Cosmic Soul and Mr Lincoln are likely to race prominently just behind the leaders, while the majority of the field including King Sacre, Largy Meadow and Pure Gold will look to come from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish, as the early pace battle will set up a strong finish for closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Ailt An Chorrain and Scriabin go hard early and weaken
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will stretch the field and favour horses with a strong finishing kick. Hold-up horses with proven stamina will benefit from the strong setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters are more conservative early on
scenarios.body: A steadier gallop will make it harder for closers to make up ground and could favour those racing closer to the pace. The prominent runners will have more left for the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners weaken dramatically in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: Late closers with proven finishing ability will have maximum advantage as the race falls apart up front. Patient rides will be rewarded with a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Scriabin and Ailt An Chorrain maintain their battle to the line
scenarios.body: One of the pace-setters could steal the race if they can outlast their rival. Prominent racers just behind will also benefit from the honest tempo.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Soul switching tactics to sit closer given his recent breakthrough form could upset the pace dynamic
Ailt An Chorrain's headgear change from blinkers to cheekpieces after 67-day break may affect his pace-setting role
King Sacre's ability to handle the 9lb weight rise after his dominant Hexham victory will determine his chances
Scriabin ensuring honest early pace despite his poor 0-13 hurdles record making him vulnerable late
Largy Meadow getting the stronger pace he needs after being inconvenienced by steady tempo last time here

races.name: Perth Silver Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Classic Maestro
runners_data.note: Leading type who won gruelling 2m4f contest here in April but faces 2lb penalty and multiple pace rivals today
runners_data.comment: Some positive runs this term but he may not have his favoured soft/heavy ground
runners_data.spotlight: Battled on well to win gruelling contest here (2m4f, good) in April; that form is treated with a degree of caution but he's only 2lb higher today and this shorter trip on forecast slower ground will suit.

runners_data.name: Itwasfate
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 305-day absence with concerning run-out last time making reliability questionable
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish 9yo who is 1-5 in British points this year; ran out on latest appearance three weeks ago and it's hard to tell whether he can still be competitive off this sort of mark under rules.

runners_data.name: Newtown Rambler
runners_data.note: Front-runner wearing first-time cheekpieces and tongue-tie refitted after recent course and distance success
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish; hurdles winner in headgear for this yard in March; fair chase form; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Bounced back to form with hurdle win in first-time cheekpieces/refitted tongue-tie in March, his second start for Adrian Keatley, and made all over C&D (good to soft) when back over fences last month; obvious contender.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with poor strike-rate but perfectly positioned tactically for this pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Not best of strike rates (both wins over C&D); not jump well here last time; bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Has modest strike-rate (2-41 under all codes) and was behind Newtown Rambler and Hypotenus when fourth of seven over C&D good to soft) last month but is now 1lb lower than for last summer's convincing C&D (good) win, and can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Leading type in excellent form with quick turnaround from Tuesday's hurdles run potentially taking toll
runners_data.comment: Went 2-2 over fences at Plumpton week ago; back hurdling off 5lb lower mark so a player
runners_data.spotlight: Launched chasing career with wins at Stratford (2m1f, good to firm) and Plumpton (2m1f, good) last month, and also ran well when second over hurdles on Tuesday; evidently in very good nick but current chase mark asks a question of him, and today's forecast slower ground is probably not ideal.

runners_data.name: Hypotenus
runners_data.note: Free-going front-runner well beaten on stable debut but previous form suggests capability at this level
runners_data.comment: Taunton chase win for Joe Tickle; wind op since; could bounce back from poor run last time
runners_data.spotlight: Free-goer who often makes the running; well beaten when last of three on debut for Neil Mulholland in April but last month's third of seven behind Newtown Rambler over C&D (good to soft) was more encouraging, and he may yet have more to offer for his new stable.

races.paceDynamic: Classic Maestro, Captain Cool, Newtown Rambler and Hypotenus all have leading tendencies creating a guaranteed strong gallop from the outset. With four confirmed front-runners in a six-horse field, the pace will be relentless and stamina-sapping over this testing 2m trip. Only Garde Des Champs sits as a genuine hold-up horse while Itwasfate typically races prominently. This fierce early pace and small field heavily favours the lone closer Garde Des Champs who can pick up the pieces, while the pace battle will compromise the multiple leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners engage in their expected early battle
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop will tire the leaders and create perfect conditions for Garde Des Champs to sweep past in the closing stages. His hold-up style is perfectly suited to capitalize when the pace burns out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strongest Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Classic Maestro or Newtown Rambler can dictate terms and see off rivals
scenarios.body: One of the more experienced leaders proves too tough and stays on strongly when the others weaken. Their superior class tells despite the pace pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Itwasfate can avoid the early pace battle while staying handy
scenarios.body: Sitting just behind the leaders allows him to avoid the worst of the early exchanges while maintaining striking position. He can then pounce when the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Speed Holds Out
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides faster than expected reducing stamina demands
scenarios.body: The pace becomes less punishing allowing one of the quicker leaders to maintain their advantage. Captain Cool's recent form suggests he could be the beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Captain Cool attempting quick double after Tuesday's exertions may find the pace battle too demanding
Itwasfate's reliability after running out three weeks ago and long absence creates major question marks
Newtown Rambler and Classic Maestro both from same stable could compromise each other in pace battle
Garde Des Champs needs strong pace to set up his closing kick against better-rated rivals
Hypotenus settling better for new connections could make him more effective than recent debut suggests

races.name: Perth Gold Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: The Real Whacker
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with class but 57 days off and pulled up last time in the Grand National
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on peak efforts but those past glories may now be too distant
runners_data.spotlight: Now well handicapped judged on peak efforts, but his form during the last 12 months lacks substance; pulled up in the Grand National last time on his return to fences.

runners_data.name: Light N Strike
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who should improve for his recent comeback fourth after 193 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Back from 193 days off when a 16l fourth to Somespring Special at Newton Abbot (2m5f) and ran as though that race would bring him on; that was his best effort yet since leaving Emma Lavelle, for whom he was competitive off higher marks; trip/ground fine.

runners_data.name: Magna Sam
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying lightweight 142lbs but hasn't recaptured his Edinburgh National form
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Edinburgh National over an extended 3m7f at Musselburgh in 2023 and 2025 (both good to soft); has not recaptured his form in his last three races and now returns from further wind surgery; 6lb out of the weights.

runners_data.name: Riskintheground
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in career-best form on good ground with Harry Skelton's tactical nous
runners_data.comment: It was never in much doubt at Haydock despite the neck margin; only up 4lb
runners_data.spotlight: Good ground is key to him, though good to soft is acceptable; after signs of a revival at the Cheltenham Festival he duly delivered in a competitive 2m4f handicap at Haydock, winning cosily despite narrow margin of victory; the 4lb rise seemed generous and when beaten at Uttoxeter he bumped into the talented Glengouly on a good day; all his best form is at shorter, so stamina would be the principal concern.

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: Prominent runner hitting career-best RPRs with recent Kelso win showing his current form
runners_data.comment: Not as good as he was but has still won two of his last four races; raised 5lb for Kelso
runners_data.spotlight: Career bests on the RPR front in his last two races, winning at Kelso (2m5f) and close up at Aintree (2m4f; again on good); could run well, though a nagging concern that he didn't appear to stay 3m when he tried it once before (at this track).

runners_data.name: Statuario
runners_data.note: Prominent runner seeking hat-trick in this race with seven course wins already to his name
runners_data.comment: Second in this race in 2025; two C&D wins on good since, latest in September; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Seeking a hat-trick in this race and on the back of a seventh course success in April when he dead-heated over this trip; not handicapped out of it after just a 3lb rise, for all that he's never defied this high a mark in the past.

runners_data.name: Somespring Special
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with back-to-back wins and excellent good ground record under Hobbs
runners_data.comment: Made it 5-16 over fences when scoring at Newton Abbot (2m5f); respected back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Has enhanced her good strike-rate over fences with back-to-back wins at Newton Abbot (2m5f) and Bangor (3m; again on good); it was harder work last time after a 6lb rise and she now has another 5lb to contend with, though last time was her first go over this far.

runners_data.name: Duffle Coat
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent form but Elliott's 7/81 strike-rate suggests others preferred
runners_data.comment: No show on comeback run in Irish National; hard to be confident in although ground to suit
runners_data.spotlight: Only 1-20 over fences, the win coming in the 3m Mayo National in 2024 (good ground); finished a fine second in the Galway Plate that summer but he's been underperforming for a while now and belatedly tries a tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Walk On Quest
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won easily at Kelso but loses key jockey Jack Power for Derek Fox
runners_data.comment: Won 4 handicaps 2 seasons ago; sound run when beaten a nose over C&D latest; contender
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 5-12 over fences when readily taking care of two rivals over a similar trip at Kelso a month ago (good; made most); only 3lb higher but without Jack Power's 5lb claim, so at this level he's probably in need of his best form yet.

runners_data.name: Stans The Man
runners_data.note: Natural leader on hat-trick seeking to bounce back from close third in this race last year
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2025 and returned to form at end of last season; high on the list
runners_data.spotlight: On a hat-trick when a fairly close third in this last year and he returns off a 4lb lower mark, and in a solid run of form; enters the reckoning.

races.paceDynamic: Stans The Man will dictate terms as the lone natural leader, likely setting a controlled gallop over this extended trip. The Real Whacker, Magna Sam, Statuario, Breizh River and Walk On Quest will create a packed prominent group, with traffic dangers inevitable when the field bunches approaching the business end. Light N Strike, Riskintheground, Somespring Special and Duffle Coat must be produced from off the pace through what could become a cavalry charge. This tactical setup strongly favours the hold-up horses who can avoid the early scrimmaging and find clear racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group creates traffic problems and the pace stays steady
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade get a perfect setup to sweep past a bunched field, with Somespring Special and Riskintheground ideally positioned for their trainers' tactical expertise. Light N Strike's fresher legs after his prep run make him dangerous late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can secure a clear run and the pace doesn't collapse
scenarios.body: Breizh River or Statuario use their career-best form to dominate from their forward positions, with the hold-up horses unable to make sufficient ground. The winner comes from those tracking Stans The Man throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stans Sets Honest Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Stans The Man maintains a strong tempo that stretches the field
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop finds out the stamina of the field over this extended trip, allowing a proven stayer like Walk On Quest to emerge late. Those who race too prominently early pay the price for their exertions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and it becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race turns into a muddling affair that suits a horse getting weight like Magna Sam or allows The Real Whacker's class to shine through despite his recent struggles. Form lines become irrelevant in a slowly-run tactical battle.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems in the prominent group with The Real Whacker, Magna Sam, Statuario, Breizh River and Walk On Quest all wanting similar positions
Monitor Somespring Special's jumping under pressure as she attempts back-to-back wins in a stronger field
Check if Stans The Man maintains his recent front-running tactics or gets headed early by the prominent brigade
Watch Light N Strike's stamina reserves over this extended trip on his second start back from a long absence
Observe if The Real Whacker shows ring-rust early having been off since his Grand National pull-up

races.name: Malcolm Group Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Buy Some Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up hurdler making chase debut at 8 years old, 25 days since last run could leave him short of peak fitness
runners_data.comment: Ex-pointer; won twice over 3m here in 2024; creditable third over 2m4f here latest; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Raced exclusively over hurdles since finishing second in Cartmel hunter chase on rules debut in spring 2024; caused 50-1 shock at 2025 Punchestown festival and has been placed twice in today's headgear combination here this spring (2m4f/3m2f); contender if able to transfer that form to fences.

runners_data.name: Inis Oirr
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner with hold-up style but generally disappointing form since February 2024 success
runners_data.comment: Back to form with a C&D win last month but not sure to be in the same mood again
runners_data.spotlight: Generally disappointing since winning valuable marathon in February 2024 but won off much-reduced mark over C&D (good) in April and also ran well when second behind a progressive rival here last month; considered.

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with back-to-back wins, hold-up style perfectly suited to likely tactical pace
runners_data.comment: Dug deep at Perth (2m4f; from 4lb lower) latest; blinkers newly applied & claimer ridden.
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice over C&D before keeping on well to win three-finisher contest here (2m4f, good to soft) last month; fourth win over fences came with first-time blinkers (instead of cheekpieces) at Hexham (3m) yesterday evening when he got up close home; respected if he turns out quickly again.

runners_data.name: Settle Down Jill
runners_data.note: Hunter chase winner in good nick but faces career-high mark and significant step up in class
runners_data.comment: Fair form in hunter chases but held by Whatdeawant on last month's Hexham form
runners_data.spotlight: Looked in very good nick when readily winning Kelso hunter chase (2m7f, good) for his owner-trainer last month but faces quite daunting assignment off career-high mark on this return to a handicap; now in the care of Tristan Davidson.

runners_data.name: Ira Hayes
runners_data.note: Sole front runner will control the gallop but may have been fortunate in last win, visor first time suggests connections seeking improvement
runners_data.comment: Fortunate when winning last month but with respected stable and unexposed over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Almost certainly fortunate when winning Tramore beginners' chase (2m5f, good to yielding) in April, given he was in fourth (albeit close up) when the front three came to grief two out, but ran big race when clear second in Market Rasen handicap (3m, good) last month and features prominently in calculations here.

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: Veteran with excellent course record but well beaten in hurdle return last month after layoff
runners_data.comment: Solid record over fences here - four wins at 3m - which does at least offer some hope.
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who gained four of his six chase wins over C&D and is versatile regarding ground; well beaten when 50-1 for 2m4f hurdle here last month, after a layoff, but that was also the case before he bounced back to form and finished second in this race a year ago; can't be ignored.

runners_data.name: Neon Diamond
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from top stable but lacks recent chase form and showing no progression this season
runners_data.comment: 1-7 over hurdles, beaten off 115 in first h'cap chase, may do better if rain arrives
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make any further progress since easily winning Kilarney maiden hurdle (2m7f, yielding to soft) in first-time cheekpieces last summer and was well held when upped to 3m2f for handicap chase debut in April (her fourth run over fences); that said, her stable's runners are always respected here.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Non-runner with hold-up style who fades in finish according to profile
runners_data.comment: Two wins in points last autumn, more recent form has been less encouraging
runners_data.spotlight: Dual point winner who came good under rules with front-running success in Wexford hunter chase (2m7f, good to yielding; refitted cheekpieces) last month; faces tougher opposition here, having recently changed hands for £17,000, but it will be interesting to see what Dan Skelton can do with him.

races.paceDynamic: Ira Hayes is the only confirmed front runner and will set a steady, uncontested gallop in this small field. With six hold-up horses (Buy Some Time, Inis Oirr, Sir Carnegie, Settle Down Jill, Wasdell Dundalk, Muskerry Rock) and only one prominent runner (Neon Diamond) to potentially apply pressure, Ira Hayes will dictate terms throughout. The lack of early pace will create a tactical affair with horses queuing up behind the leader before a sprint finish over the final half-mile. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can quicken late, as the sustainable early gallop will leave plenty in reserve for those with finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Ira Hayes sets an easy lead with no pressure from Neon Diamond
scenarios.body: The uncontested gallop allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and unleash late kicks, with the best finishers sweeping past a tiring leader. Sir Carnegie and Settle Down Jill benefit most from this tactical setup given their recent form and ability to quicken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Steals March
scenarios.trigger: If Ira Hayes quickens turning for home before the field reacts
scenarios.body: The front runner exploits the lack of early pace pressure by injecting tempo when it matters, catching the hold-up horses napping. Ira Hayes builds an unassailable lead while the field struggles to respond to the sudden acceleration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactics Pay
scenarios.trigger: If Neon Diamond tracks Ira Hayes closely and applies sustained pressure
scenarios.body: The Gordon Elliott-trained runner forces a stronger gallop that suits his prominent style while compromising the hold-up horses' finishing kicks. This tactical pressure creates the perfect setup for horses that can sustain a longer drive rather than relying on sprint finishes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Veteran Experience Counts
scenarios.trigger: If Wasdell Dundalk's course knowledge proves decisive in a slowly-run tactical affair
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old's familiarity with Perth's unique demands and proven course record allows him to time his challenge perfectly when others struggle with the track's nuances. His four previous course wins demonstrate an ability to handle Perth's specific tactical requirements.

watchPoints.text: Ira Hayes dictating an uncontested lead - if no pressure applied early, hold-up horses will have perfect tactical setup
Neon Diamond's early positioning - any forward move to pressure the leader changes the entire race dynamic significantly
Sir Carnegie's jumping under pressure - back-to-back winner but needs to handle extended trip without mistakes
Settle Down Jill's class adjustment - hunter chase winner stepping up significantly in grade off career-high mark
Weather conditions on race day - any ground change from current good could impact several runners' chances

races.name: IM Group Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Maillot Blanc
runners_data.note: Defending champion with strong recent form on good ground, prominent style suits if he gets clear run from forward position
runners_data.comment: 3m Perth winner last summer; sound placed runs on last two starts; very much in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race last term and better form this spring, all on good ground; dead-heated for first at Kelso (2m5f) last time, which has pushed him up 3lb to his highest mark since 2024 but he looks much more likely than most of these to give his running; should be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Our Girl Sal
runners_data.note: 364 days off but won well last time for new trainer, prominent runner who needs to avoid traffic in congested field
runners_data.spotlight: Got up on the line at Kelso (3m2f) in May 2025 on second start for Paul Robson, opening her rules account; made the running when well beaten behind Maillot Blanc in this race last year, however, and not seen since; has changed hands and now has first run for Adam Nichol, with a tongue-tie (tried twice in 2024) restored.

runners_data.name: Stiletto
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with C&D win last year, out of form recently but class horse if Sophie Leech can find revival
runners_data.comment: 8yo who has been well held in last three runs and needs a major revival after wind surgery
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times (2m2f-3m) in June-September last year, off today's mark over C&D on last occasion; out of form on last four outings, however, and a major revival is needed on this second start after wind surgery; tongue-tie (last used in 2024) returns.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Previous course winner who stays well, hold-up style perfect for this race shape but form inconsistent at age 11
runners_data.comment: Three-time Perth winner (2m4f-3m); well beaten on Wednesday on first run since November
runners_data.spotlight: This race in 2024 is among his three Perth wins from 23 visits; latest win was last July over C&D again from 2lb higher than today and that was his second run after a break, the same scenario which presents itself today; needs a second look but others are preferred for the win.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner gives him tactical advantage, but poor hurdle record (0-20) and recent poor form concern
runners_data.comment: C&D winner (chasing debut) last October; well beaten on both subsequent starts; risky.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-20 over hurdles but won here (3m, soft) on chase debut last October; three major backward steps this spring prompt caution on this return to hurdling, with cheekpieces (tried often as hurdler last year) reinstated.

runners_data.name: Shighness
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with no recent win, 5lb claimer rides but unseated last time suggests confidence issues
runners_data.comment: On a handy mark and back to some form on last hurdles start so hard to rule out.
runners_data.spotlight: No win since a chase early in 2024; only occasional echoes of that form and she was held when unseating on the turn at Hexham on latest start.

runners_data.name: Leader Wing
runners_data.note: Promising prominent runner but 0-15 over hurdles for current connections, 79 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Effective over C&D; creditable third to Big Storm Brewing latest; hurdles score is 0-14
runners_data.spotlight: Won a bumper in May 2024; 0-15 as a hurdler for Gillian Boanas but had his share of seconds and thirds, including over 3m; £12,500 sale in March was quickly followed by wind surgery and, although usual headgear is dispensed with, new trainer Dan Skelton has something to work with; one to note.

runners_data.name: Jakana
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts her in traffic danger zone, partial chase revival but poor recent hurdle form
runners_data.comment: 12l fourth on last month's Perth chasing debut, shaping as if needing further than 3m.
runners_data.spotlight: Partial revival on chase debut here (3m, good) in April but she did not shine at Cartmel one month later; has plenty of form to make this look an attractive mark but there are doubts on this return to hurdling.

runners_data.name: Creadan Grace
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner with strong 3m win last time, hold-up style ideal for expected race shape
runners_data.spotlight: Upped to 3m for a last-gasp win in 20-runner race at Down Royal in October; respectable fourth of 18 under James Smith at Punchestown (again 3m on good to yielding) last month confirms her in serious calculations.

runners_data.name: Reagrove Lord
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 400-day break, needs to improve but lighter weight helps
runners_data.spotlight: 0-17 as hurdler but plenty of minor honours, including C&D; needs to improve upon last month's fourth at Hexham but that was his first run for 400 days, so he may well build on that; case can be made off career-low mark.

runners_data.name: Myfavouritesister
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden who struggled on chase debut, 67 days off and 3lb claimer takes over
runners_data.comment: Consistent maiden hurdler; off since September but no forlorn hope now going chasing
runners_data.spotlight: 13-race maiden, with nine of those races over hurdles; did little on chase debut last time (after six months off) but several bits of hurdle form last year, including over C&D, give her a place chance.

runners_data.name: Luminaries
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won previous races in spring months, 143 days since last run major concern
runners_data.comment: Needs to get back on track but he's on a dangerous mark and is 3-3 over C&D
runners_data.spotlight: Tried chasing last autumn and did not show much back over hurdles in the winter on last two outings; 4-20 overall as a hurdler, with all four wins in March-May 2025, but there have to be questions at the moment.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with each-way claims, consistent recent form but needs to find improvement
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent, but a leading player if reproducing his latest third at Exeter last month.
runners_data.spotlight: 2m4f hurdle and 2m7f chase winner (once each) from 35 races; his last win was in 2024 but bits of form this year, including penultimate start, give him an each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Breaking Ground
runners_data.note: Handicap debut over much longer trip, fading tendency and poor form make her vulnerable despite hold-up style
runners_data.comment: Signs of only a little ability and needs to find significant improvement in tongue-tie
runners_data.spotlight: This is her handicap debut and a major step up in trip, but there have been signs of only a little ability; tongue tied on latest start and a hood (tried four starts back, pulled up) is reinstated.

races.paceDynamic: Burgundy Man will take them along at a sensible gallop in this 3m contest, with no other confirmed front-runners to pressure him early. The prominent brigade of Maillot Blanc, Our Girl Sal, Leader Wing, Jakana, Reagrove Lord and Watchoutitscookie creates significant congestion behind the leader, setting up potential traffic problems turning for home. This moderate early pace followed by prominent congestion strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the scramble and produce late runs when the pace lifts from 2 furlongs out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prosper
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man sets moderate fractions and the prominent group gets bunched up approaching the business end
scenarios.body: The pace will quicken dramatically from 2 out as the field compresses, allowing patient riders to weave through and pick up the pieces. Stiletto and Creadan Grace have the class to capitalise from their hold-up positions when others have shot their bolt.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners can secure clear runs and the pace stays honest throughout
scenarios.body: Maillot Blanc's superior class tells as he gets first run from his forward position, with Our Girl Sal potentially following him through. The hold-up horses find the moderate pace hasn't set up their usual finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Burgundy Man Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If no horse can sustain a challenge to Burgundy Man's honest gallop over this stamina-sapping trip
scenarios.body: The leader's relentless rhythm proves too much for the closers on this good ground over 3m. His previous course win over fences shows he handles Perth's demands, and the patient ride allows him to see out the trip strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes multiple horses to be hampered or forced wide around the turn
scenarios.body: The pace collapses as several fancied runners get into trouble, allowing a patient outsider like Luminaries or Myfavouritesister to steal through on the rails. Breaking Ground could even benefit from the mayhem despite her limitations.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic jam developing 2 furlongs out as Maillot Blanc, Our Girl Sal, Leader Wing, Jakana, Reagrove Lord and Watchoutitscookie all converge
Burgundy Man's jumping under pressure - 0-20 hurdle record suggests he may not handle race pressure despite tactical advantage
Stiletto's revival bid after four poor runs - hold-up style suits but needs significant bounce back to form
Creadan Grace and Dalileo getting competitive rides from 5lb claimers in heavy ground conditions that could test stamina further
Breaking Ground's stamina test on handicap debut - major step up to 3m could expose limitations or unlock improvement
